title: General Process of Using Modular Mode
content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template ▶ Add Patterns or Garments ▶ Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes ▶ Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes ▶ Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for creating and managing your own Pattern database using the Modular Mode, ensuring a streamlined design and building process.

title: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### **Objective** Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. ** Location** Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular Configurator** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ **Modular Configurator** → Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. → Folders appear in order. 3. Select a desired Garment category folder. → Modular Structure file is displayed. 4. Select a desired Modular Structure file. → All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 5. Select a desired Block. → The Blocks are replaced accordingly. 6. Modify the design as desired and complete the 3D Garment.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of selecting and customizing garment design blocks using the Modular Configurator tool.

title: Invert Selection
content: ### **Objective** Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. ** Location** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) ▶**Invert Selection** Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶**Invert Selection** ** Operation** 1. Select Patterns that will be deselected. 2. Follow the indicated guideline as below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) ▶ **Invert Selection** Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ **Invert Selection** → All Patterns that were selected are deselected, while the remaining patterns are selected.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a clear guide on how to invert the selection of patterns in a user interface, allowing them to easily switch between selected and unselected patterns.

title: Edit Measurement
content: ### **Objective** Edit avatar measurements. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab** ### **Operation ** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Measure Tab**** ** → The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. 2. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. **Name** | Rename the measurement. | **Basic Length** | Check the measurement's basic length. ---|---|---|--- **Measurement Type** | Change the measurement type. | **Surface Length** | Check the surface length of the measurement. **Measurement Information** | Check the measurement's information. | **Show** | Show or hide the selected measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a user-friendly interface for editing and managing avatar measurements within the Avatar Editor.

title: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: **Objective** Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. **※ Note:** For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that [Skin Offset](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002227387) is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. **Location** Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Collision** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This webpage provides a guide on adjusting the Simulation Thickness for garment patterns to optimize collision limits and achieve smoother simulations in garment design.

title: Delete All Overlapping Points
content: **Objective** Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When importing *.dxf files created in other CAD programs or cutting Patterns in CLO, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by CLO. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Delete All Overlapping Points** → All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with a quick guide on how to delete overlapping points in CLO patterns to ensure smooth editing and movement of their designs.

title: Fabric Information Preview
content: **Fabric Information PreviewYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tUklcQKYA94 ** **-** Preview fabric information in the Library Window. \- Hover the mouse over the fabric (.zfab) file in the Library Window for about 0.5 second. \- The preview of fabric information will appear on the right. \- Only fabric (.zfab) files saved in v.3.1.0 or higher versions can see the preview. \- To preview fabrics saved in previous versions, save the same fabric (.zfab) files in v.3.1.0 or higher versions. Then, open updated fabric (.zfab) files.
content_description: Discover how to easily preview fabric information directly in the Library Window by hovering over .zfab files, ensuring compatibility with version 3.1.0 or higher.

title: Replace as Pattern Outline
content: **Replace as Pattern OutlineYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1CSah6-I3uc** **-** Swap Internal Line and Pattern Outline to replace Internal Line as Pattern Outline. \- Select **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D Window. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select Internal Line and Pattern Outline to be swapped. \- Selected Internal Line and Pattern Outline will be highlighted in yellow. \- Right click on the selected lines to access a pop-up menu. \- Select **Replace as Pattern Outline.** \- The selected Pattern Outline will be replaced with the selected Internal Line as original Pattern Outline will appear as Baseline.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to replace an Internal Line with a Pattern Outline in a 2D design using the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Pleats Fold
content: **List of Contents** Pleats Fold Using Pleats Fold Pleats Fold Options **Pleats Fold** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZYJlNzBP3BM \- Auto assign fold angles based on the direction of the pleats. \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar. **Using Pleats Fold** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gVDbq6f6VRI \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Click on the pattern to designate the start point of the pleats direction. Then, drag the mouse towards the direction the pleats will be folded. \- Double click to complete the guide line. \- Make sure to encompass all internal lines that fold angles should be assigned to. \- The Pleats Fold Window will appear. **Pleats Fold Options** * **Pleats Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ybOSk9LBLRU ** \- Select the desired pleats type among following options: knife pleats, box pleats, and accordion pleats. * **Options YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULrUF0DfnwY**** ** * **REVERSE DIRECTION -**Change the fold direction of the pleats * **FOLD ANGLE** \- Set fold angle range that will be applied to the pleats pattern. \- Choose among Preset or enter the desired value. * **NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS** \- Decide whether two or three internal lines will be included per pleats. \- If internal lines that are supposed to have 180° fold angles are not established within the pleats pattern, select two for NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS. \- After the adjusting the options, hit OK. \- The outside folds will be highlighted in red whereas the inside folds will be highlighted in green. \- The pleats pattern will be folded based on the settings when the Simulation is activated. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to utilizing the Pleats Fold tool, featuring tutorials, options, and techniques for creating various pleat styles in your designs.

title: Tack on Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Tack on Avatar Creating Tack on Avatar **Tack on Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8TdqE66uRH0 \- Use tack to affix a part of the 3D Garment to Avatar. \- Select the **Tack on Avatar** tool from the 3D Toolbar. **Creating Tack on Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sNO5wQwa_J8 \- Select the **Tack on Avatar** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a black guide point appears. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D garment. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent and the Avatar becomes visible. \- A dashed black line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the desired part of the Avatar where the 3D Garment should be affixed to. \- The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for using the "Tack on Avatar" tool in 3D garment design, featuring step-by-step instructions and instructional video links.

title: Tack
content: **List of Contents** Tack Creating Tack **Tack** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6FDcB7Y2eZY \- Use tack to affix parts of the 3D Garment together. \- Select the **Tack** tool from the 3D Toolbar. **Creating Tack** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tr5m1mIZgBY \- Select the **Tack** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a purple guide point appears. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D Garment. \- A dashed purple line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the desired part of the 3D garment to designate the attaching point. \- The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide and instructional videos on how to use the Tack tool to affix parts of a 3D garment in a design software.

title: Edit Tack
content: **List of Contents** Edit Tack Moving Tack Adjusting Tack Property Deleting Tack **Edit Tack** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-9VrnnCJvY \- Adjust or delete previously created Tack. \- Select the **Edit Tack** tool from the 3D toolbar. **Moving Tack** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SNFa0lLA51Q \- Tack Can be moved both in the 2D Window and the 3D Window. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent when the **Edit Tack** tool is selected. \- To move the Tack, click and drag the point to be moved. \- Release the mouse to complete the adjustment. \- In the 2D Window, only the Tack on the 2D Pattern can be moved if were to edit an Avatar Tack. **Adjusting Tack Property** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNIzowYelmU \- Select the **Edit Tack** tool from the 3D toolbar and select the tack to be edited in either the 2D or the 3D Window. \- The selected tack’s property will appear in the Property Editor. \- Enter the desired value for **THREAD LENGTH** to adjust the thread length joining the tack. **Deleting Tack** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vg7FwQyUqWM \- Select the Edit Tack tool from the 3D Toolbar and hover over the tack to be deleted. \- Right click to access the pop-up menu. \- Click DELETE. \- Or, select the tack to be deleted and hit Delete key on the keyboard. \- The selected tack will be deleted. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions and video tutorials for editing, moving, adjusting properties, and deleting tacks in both 2D and 3D garment design environments.

title: Poly Pen
content: **Poly Pen** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y3CuVVzEvlk ** **-** Draw polygons or curves to request design modifications in the Comment Mode. \- Comment Mode ▶ Main Menu ▶ **Poly Pen.** \- Use the Poly Pen to address changes or garment information. * Create Segment To create a segment, click and drag from a start point. Double click to complete the segment. * Create Polygon To create a polygon, click on a start point and click to shape a polygon. Double click the start point to complete the polygon. * Create Curve After starting a segment, hold down the Ctrl key and click the next point. A curve point is added. Double click to complete the curves.

title: Custom View
content: **List of Contents** Custom View Adding and Applying Custom View Saving and Opening Custom View Deleting Custom View Renaming Custom View Managing Custom View Overwrite Custom View (ver4.1.0) Delete All Custom View (ver4.1.0) **Custom ViewYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLN1Owoo-ys** \- Add frequently used view and easily apply to the 3D Window. \- Right click on the 3D Window to access a pop-up menu. Select **CUSTOM VIEW**. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu – Display – View Point – **CUSTOM VIEW**. ** Adding and Applying Custom ViewYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NlUuy8QFe5s** \- Navigate to Main Menu – Display – View Point – **CUSTOM VIEW**. content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing Custom Views in a 3D window, detailing how to add, apply, save, open, delete, rename, and overwrite views, along with instructional videos for each process.

title: Open/Save Trim
content: **List of Contents** Save Trim Open Trim **Save Trim** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pecYUUmP0Y \- Save OBJ files as Trims. \- Trim files can be previewed in CLO Library and glue to 3D Garments once they are imported to the 3D window. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** When loading an OBJ file, opt Load as Trim. \- Select the desired OBJ file when saving if there are multiple OBJs loaded to the file you are working on. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Trim** The OBJ file is saved as a Trim file. ** Open Trim** * **Open with File Open Window ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j1Bi2qriJBw \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶**Trim** When the Open Trim window appears, designate where the Trim will be placed in the 3D window with the Position option. \- When you select Original, the Trim will be placed where it was when the file was saved. \- When you select **Reset (0,0),** the Trim will be placed at the center of the 3D grid. * **Open with the Livrary Window ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p99fiwoyNsA \- When the Trim file is hovered over in the Library window, its preview appears. \- Double click or click and drag the Trim file to the 3D window in order to open the file. \- When the Open Trim window appears, designate where the Trim will be placed in the 3D window with the Position option. \- When you select Original, the Trim will be placed where it was when the file was saved. \- When you select **Reset (0,0),** the Trim will be placed at the center of the 3D grid. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on saving and opening Trim files in CLO, including step-by-step instructions and helpful YouTube video links for easy reference.

title: Pleats Sewing
content: **List of Contents** Pleats Sewing Using Pleats Sewing **Pleats Sewing YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mgS-cXtYKmI ** \- Easily sew pleats pattern to another pattern. \- Select the **Pleats Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. **Using Pleats Sewing YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ND8L4PN8pG0** \- In order to use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew pleats pattern to its paired pattern, both patterns should have Internal Lines with the same offset. Also, the ratio between the pleats pattern’s number of lines, including both Pattern outlines and Internal Lines, and the paired pattern’s number of lines should be 3:1. \- Additionally, segment points should be added to the intersection of Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. \- After achieving above conditions, select the Pleats Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Be careful and always establish the sewing line on the paired pattern first. The **Pleats Sewing** tool would not work properly when such caution is not taken. \- Click on the either end of the Pattern outline where the first half of the pleats sewing line will be established on. The sewing direction should be equal to the pleats direction. \- Drag the mouse cursor towards the sewing direction and click again to complete the first half of the sewing line. \- Then, hover the mouse over the pleats pattern’s Pattern Outline. click on the either end of the pattern to designate the start point of the second half of the pleats sewing line. \- Drag the mouse towards the sewing direction and click again to complete. \- The second half of the sewing line’s direction must be the same as the first half of the sewing line’s direction. \- Now the pleats sewing lines are completed. \- Please use the **Free Sewing** tool when sewing accordion pleats. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide and helpful resources for mastering the Pleats Sewing technique, including step-by-step instructions and instructional videos.

title: Automated Arrangement Point Creation
content: **Automated Arrangement Point Creation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9NPKXBmTUlQ \- Load an Avatar by navigating to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ. \- **Automatically Add Arrangement Points** option under Load OBJ window ▶ Load as Avatar is selected by default. \- Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes are automatically created sized to the loaded OBJ. **※Note****: ** This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. ‘Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose of A-pose’
content_description: Discover how to effortlessly create automated arrangement points for your 3D avatars by following our step-by-step guide and video tutorial.
